title: parse_certificate_issuer_dn: opaque error for 'no directoryName'
description:
Location: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, parse_certificate_issuer_dn() (lines 989-1008)

When the certificateIssuer CRL entry extension contains only non-DN GeneralNames (e.g., only rfc822Name or URI), the function fabricates a DER error:

  Err(Error::CrlParseError(crate::DerError::new(der::Error::new(
      der::ErrorKind::Failed,
      der::Length::ZERO,
  ))))

This returns a CrlParseError whose Display message is something like 'DER error at offset 0' — not actionable for someone debugging why a specific CRL entry was rejected. The actual situation is 'we parsed the certificateIssuer extension successfully, but found no directoryName among the GeneralNames', which is semantically different from a parse failure.

What goes wrong: an operator seeing 'CRL parse error: [...] at offset 0' in logs will investigate a DER formatting issue that does not exist. A comment at line 999-1003 explains the real situation, but that context does not reach the error consumer. A dedicated Error variant (e.g., CertificateIssuerNoDn) or at minimum a more descriptive DerError message would eliminate the red herring.
